headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: ComfyUI can touch local model files and has vendor-only egress, while the paired content-writing agent is broad-egress but has no documented shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between agent_a and agent_b. agent_a has no I/O surfaces or runnable path, while agent_b exposes files only for model assets and no clipboard/stdin/stdout or MCP bridge. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
IF agent_a is made runnable and its outputs are parsed as instructions by agent_b, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not add shared clipboard or queue plumbing.
Run agent_b with instruction/content separation for any imported text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags before any cross-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b touches model files and workflows, and agent_a has broad network egress. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace, but if any local files from agent_b are exposed to agent_a, agent_a could transmit them off-box. Uncertainty pushes this above low because agent_a's egress is broad and agent_b's file surfaces are explicit.
conditions: IF agent_a is given access to any ComfyUI model, workflow, or seed files, leakage becomes plausible.
IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace, reassess for shared-data exposure.
mitigations: Do not mount ComfyUI model directories into agent_a's environment.
Restrict agent_a egress with an allowlist or proxy.
Store workflows and seeds in a separate directory with read permissions only for agent_b.
requires-engineering: add per-agent storage isolation and audit logs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or shell capabilities, and agent_b cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. That blocks the usual write-write conflict pathways. The only overlap is indirect network use, so conflict risk is limited and not dangerous by default.
conditions: IF agent_a is later granted filesystem or git write access, conflict risk increases.
IF agent_b is run with additional write permissions outside the profile, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep agent_a read-only with no workspace writes.
Leave agent_b's write and git permissions disabled.
Use separate output directories for each agent.
requires-engineering: add a lock manager if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a content-writing agent, so its outputs can be treated as authoritative text, while agent_b is an image-generation system that can consume workflows and produce downstream artifacts. Even without a documented direct handoff, the pair can form an unverified content-to-workflow chain, creating moderate cascading-error risk.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-generated prompts or workflows without review, cascading errors become likely.
IF agent_a's text is used to configure image-generation jobs, reassess upward.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any workflow execution.
Require schema validation for prompts and workflows.
Compare generated outputs against a known-good template.
requires-engineering: add automated verification of agent_a outputs before agent_b acts on them.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. agent_b is offline-capable and agent_a is an open-source list with no data classes touched, so compliance exposure is limited to deployment choices rather than inherent behavior. The other agent is cited because the pairwise deployment context matters, but no breach is evidenced.
conditions: IF deployment routes EU PII or PHI through either agent, reassess compliance obligations.
IF retention or logging policies differ across the two runtimes, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through either agent.
Document retention and logging settings for both runtimes.
Keep ComfyUI offline unless a DPA-approved endpoint is used.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for regulated-data workflows.
